principles: Every article must solve a concrete reader problem and add practical value.
No article is published merely to increase volume or target keywords.
Every image must support the section or heading immediately before it; decorative or generic images fail review.
Repeated images across recent articles fail the image gate unless there is a documented editorial reason.
The website must be visually coherent: typography, spacing, cards, images, navigation and mobile layout are reviewed as one system.
Existing published articles are subject to repair; publication does not imply editorial approval.
Two high-quality articles per day is the target only after the repair gates are green.
Gemini may generate drafts, but it cannot bypass the editorial, image, duplicate-content or deployment gates.
A failed gate stops publication rather than lowering the quality threshold.
